newsitem.title: USA: Fleet Q1 net up 30 pct on operating basis.
newsitem.headline: Fleet Q1 net up 30 pct on operating basis.

text.p: Fleet Financial Group Inc Wednesday reported an 18 percent increase in first quarter profits saying earnings were up 30 percent on an operating basis.
It said net income was $311 million, or $1.10 per share, in the latest quarter compared with $264 million, or $0.94 per share a year earlier.

The bank said return on average assets and return on average common equity for the first quarter of 1997 were 1.52 percent and 18.82 percent, respectively, compared with 1.41 percent and 16.96 percent for the first quarter of 1996.
"We're delighted with Fleet's performance in the first quarter," Chief Executive Terrence Murray said.
"Earnings were up 30 percent on an operating basis after adjusting for divestiture gains in last year's first quarter. That's strong growth by any measure.
He said "We're seeing strong business opportunities across all our core businesses which are producing outstanding results on the bottom line.
"We enter 1997 with great optimism as our customer driven strategy continues to pay dividends."

Murray noted, "The introduction of our investment banking product line early last year has expanded our revenue growth prospects as well as demonstrated the broad range of capabilities across which Fleet addresses customers' changing financial needs."

Eugene McQuade, chief financial officer, said, "The earnings performance with which Fleet has started 1997 demonstrates the successful implementation of business line strategies. The improvement in our efficiency ratio to 58.8 percent reflects our continuing progress in attaining the cost reduction goal of $600 million from the acquisitions of Shawmut and NatWest."

McQuade continued, "Net interest margin rose to 5.16 percent, a 73 basis point improvement over the 4.43 percent reported in the first quarter of 1996. This margin expansion reflects the impact of the comprehensive balance sheet restructuring undertaken in 1996.
"Progress in the first quarter also includes significant sales of mutual fund and annuity products which were more than 55 percent higher than sales in the first quarter of 1996."
